package_info.why_malicious: This report does not analyze a specific malicious package, but rather discusses the widespread risk and lack of detection capabilities for software supply chain attacks, including tampering and the use of malicious or compromised third-party/open source components.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected or unauthorized modifications to software artifacts (tampering)
Introduction of malicious code via third-party or open source dependencies
Lack of verification or review of software at each stage of the development lifecycle
Release of software with known or unknown vulnerabilities
file_indicators: Unexplained changes in source code or build artifacts
Presence of dependencies or plugins not reviewed or approved
Absence of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) or incomplete SBOMs
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections during build, test, or deployment phases
Connections to known malicious or suspicious domains from CI/CD environments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement automated and continuous integrity checks for all software artifacts throughout the development lifecycle. Monitor for unauthorized changes in source code, dependencies, and build outputs. Require and review SBOMs for all releases. Use behavioral monitoring to detect unexpected network activity during build and deployment. Regularly audit and scan third-party and open source components for vulnerabilities and signs of tampering.
